Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Virgin River Complex Wild and Scenic Rivers BLM-Utah manages 11 river segments totaling 19 miles within the Virgin River drainage and all are classified as "wild". Each of the segments flows into or out of Zion National Park and a majority are within wilderness areas that were also designated in the 2009 Omnibus Public Land Management Act (Public Law 111-11). These river segments are managed under a Comprehensive Management Plan in concert with the National Park Service. The rugged terrain and lack of nearby roads makes the majority of the BLM-administered river segments difficult to access. The Virgin River and its tributaries provide a unique and intact habitat for four native fish species, including the Virgin spinedace, which only exists in the Virgin River system, and the flannelmouth sucker, desert sucker and speckled dace. The Zion stonefly (Isogenoides zionensis), an important component of the food web, is also found along the Virgin River and its tributaries. Every vaccine ingredient serves a purpose To provide immunity We become immune to (or protected from) a disease when our bodies create specific antibodies to fight that disease. Vaccines contain ingredients that help your body build this immunity . To keep the vaccine safe and long-lasting Vaccines need to be safe and effective. Certain ingredients help keep vaccines safe from contamination and toxins. Others, like stabilizers, help vaccines stay effective for a long time. To make the vaccine more effective All vaccine ingredients help to make a vaccine as effective as possible, while being safe. Ingredients like aluminum salt help boost the body's response to the vaccine. Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) A medical condition where the immune system cannot function properly and protect the body from disease. As a result, the body cannot defend itself against infections (like pneumonia). AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). This virus is spread through direct contact with the blood and body fluids of an infected individual. High risk activities include unprotected sexual intercourse and intravenous drug use (sharing needles). There is no cure for AIDS; however, research efforts to develop a vaccine are ongoing. Active immunity The production of antibodies against a specific disease by the immune system. Active immunity can be acquired in two ways, either by contracting the disease or through vaccination. It's important that children get their vaccines on time so they're protected against serious diseases. These slices are known as spectrum. Spectrum is a finite resource, and as technology advances, demand for it continues to grow, straining the supply of open frequencies. Dynamic spectrum sharing is one answer to this problem and involves allowing different users to share the same frequencies rather than giving each user an exclusive slice. The Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) band is a test of that idea. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) rules allow commercial networks to use the CBRS band (3550-3700 MHz), and share the airwaves with federal incumbents, who hold priority and have operated in the allocated band for decades. Automated Spectrum Access Systems (SAS) assign channels and power levels to commercial devices, while a separate sensor network, the Environmental Sensing Capability (ESC), watches for federal activity.

The 2021 VIUS provides data on the physical and operational characteristics of the nation’s truck population. A sample of approximately 150,000 vehicles was selected from more than 190 million private and commercially owned trucks registered with motor vehicle departments in 49 U.S. states and the District of Columbia. New Hampshire did not allow the Census Bureau access to its motor vehicle registration records, and therefore New Hampshire was not included in the VIUS data collection. pages.text: Velociraptor’s new cousin is a raptor unlike any seen before | National Geographic SCIENCE Velociraptor’s new cousin is a raptor unlike any seen before Shri rapax had bigger claws and potentially a stronger bite than its Hollywood relative. But paleontologists still don’t know the whereabouts of its head, which went missing. The newly named raptor Shri rapax was smuggled by poachers, rescued from the black market, and then, sometime following a CT-scan in 2016, its skull went missing. Photograph by Thierry Hubin, Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences By Riley Black Published July 29, 2025 Sometime before 2010, in the red sands of Mongolia’s Gobi Desert brimming with fossils, poachers excavated and stole the exquisite skeleton of a carnivorous dinosaur. They smuggled the fossil out of the country and onto the black market. It passed through private collections in Japan and England and was eventually acquired by the French fossil company Eldonia. In 2016, one of the fossil’s owners had the dinosaur’s skull and four vertebrae CT-scanned at a Belgian museum, but sometime later the head and neck went missing. Their whereabouts remain unknown to scientists. Negotiations between the fossil company, paleontologists, and government officials led to the return of the dinosaur’s body to Mongolia, where it could be cared for and studied, a raptor unlike any seen before. Now, this headless, extra-sharp relative of Velociraptor finally has a name: Shri rapax . Moonlight illuminates colorful salt domes in Iran’s Dasht-e Kavir desert, while Venus—the brightest planet in Earth’s sky—shines near the horizon. Babak Tafreshi, National Geographic Image Collection By Stefanie Waldek Published September 17, 2026 The brightest planet in our sky is putting on an especially dazzling show. On September 18, Venus will reach the greatest illuminated extent of its 2026 evening appearance, blazing low in the western sky after sunset. What makes the event especially interesting is that Venus isn’t brightest when it looks “full.” Instead, the planet peaks in brightness while appearing as a crescent through a telescope—a result of a delicate balance between how much of Venus is illuminated and how close it is to Earth. Why is Venus so bright? Venus is the brightest planet seen from Earth and typically the third-brightest natural object in our sky, behind only the sun and moon. Part of that comes down to its proximity and size: Venus is one of Earth’s nearest planetary neighbors, and it’s relatively large for a rocky planet. Close vgeorge's Diary OSM for Cities at State of the Map Latam 2026 Posted by vgeorge on 31 October 2026 in Spanish (Español) . On 29 October I presented OSM for Cities at State of the Map Latam in Ciudad de México. The project shows how well OpenStreetMap covers a kind of data in a given city, and how recently anyone touched it. The slides are online , in Spanish. Photo by Jordan Jasuta Fischer Most of the talk was a live demo with Mexico City bus stops, coloured by when each one was last edited. When I made the slides, 317 stops had been edited in the past week, almost all along a few routes in the west of the city. Someone was mapping them right then. Most of the rest had not been touched in over 90 days. That is what the platform is for, following a dataset over time instead of looking at it once. Save a dataset and it is refreshed from OSM every day, and a notification arrive by email if it changes. A city team can see when its bus stops get mapped, and a mapper can see whether anyone else is keeping their area up to date. Vector tiles are coming soon Today a dataset loads into the page as one GeoJSON file. That works for bus stops, but not for the buildings or streets of a large city, which is why those are not on the platform yet. Buildings matter most for disaster response and health planning. O OSM for Cities é um projeto de distribuição de dados abertos sobre as cidades baseado no OpenStreetMap. O objetivo é facilitar o acesso e acompanhamento dos dados produzidos pela comunidade do OSM para organizações, grupos locais e profissionais que trabalham com questões urbanas. A ideia se originou quando trabalhava em projetos de planejamento de transportes, mais ou menos quando conheci o OpenStreetMap, em 2008. Não havia cobertura de dados oficiais de vias e infraestrutura, e sempre era preciso uma fase inicial de coleta de dados, que ao fim do projeto não eram reutilizados. Hoje em dia a situação é um pouco diferente e muitas grandes cidades produzem e publicam seus dados. Mas mesmo cidades que contam com equipes técnicas focam seus recursos em conjuntos de dados críticos e dificilmente conseguem publicar e manter atualizadas informações sobre mobiliário urbano, cobertura arbórea, iluminação pública e outros elementos específicos que possam ajudar em políticas públicas. O OSM for Cities pretende ser uma ferramenta para aqueles que trabalham com este tipo de informação, complementando outras ferramentas que já existem no ecossistema do OSM, como o HOT Export Tool. Um diferencial do projeto é ser possível buscar qualquer cidade do mundo e visualizar seus dados dentro do seu limite administrativo, sem precisar de conhecimento técnico ou preparação dos dados. The Canadian rolls through some of Canada’s most serene landscapes, including the Rocky Mountains. VIA Rail Canada By Taras Grescoe Last updated August 14, 2026 We’re somewhere east of Winnipeg when I realize I’ve lost all track of time. I’ve been swaying through the corridors back to my room, through what VIA Rail staff call the Activity Car, when Carol, a veterinarian from South Dakota, asks me if I’d like to sit down with her and Trinity, from Wisconsin, to play cards. They introduce me to the rules of a game called King in the Corner. Every once in a while, I look up from the cards to take in the scene outside: a trackside grain elevator scrolling by, a red fox trotting across a farmer’s field. It’s not just that we’ve crossed the Continental Divide and two time zones. Part of the sense of timelessness comes from the slow sorcery of long-distance travel over land, aboard The Canadian , a train that still uses the same streamlined passenger cars that rolled across the country on its inaugural run on April 24, 1955. pages.text: Victory, At Last, Lesson 6 | Crash Course: American Revolution | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE CRASH COURSE Victory, At Last Lesson 6: From the battle of Monmouth to Britain’s surrender at Yorktown, Americans overcame tremendous odds to win their independence. On May 6, 1778 , George Washington’s army celebrated America’s alliance with France. Twelve days later, in British-occupied Philadelphia, musicians played “God Save the King” during a lavish tribute to the departing commander in chief, Maj. Gen. William Howe, that had fireworks and jousts between mounted officers in costume. Howe had also grown tired of the war and asked to be “relieved from this very painful service.” His successor, Lt. Gen. Henry Clinton, had orders to abandon Philadelphia and return occupying troops to New York City, thus nullifying Howe’s campaign the year before. While giving up the American capital, the British were planning to expand operations elsewhere to contend with France and target southern states. Clinton would have to hold New York while deploying troops to battle French forces in the West Indies; defend British East Florida and West Florida, which extended along the Gulf Coast to the Mississippi River; and invade Georgia and the Carolinas. Defending New York City, which the British are shown entering in 1776 in this colorized version of the original engraving (circa 1776), tied down thousands of British troops there as France entered the war against them. Introducing NPR Music's Tiny Desk (home) concerts, bringing you performances from across the country and the world. It's the same spirit — stripped-down sets, an intimate setting — just a different space. "Tiny Desk! We finally made it!" exclaimed singer-songwriter Mac Ayres as he finished his opening number, "She Won't Stay Long." I'm sure his fans will especially feel that sentiment since they've made a home in our social media feeds and YouTube comments for years now. We were well on the way to hosting Mac Ayres at our D.C. offices until we had to shut down and pivot. As we worked our way through the adjustment to Tiny Desk (home) concerts, he also needed some time to regroup. pages.text: Vinicius Jr: Real Madrid forward says transfer interest has affected form - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid in August By Marissa Thomas BBC Sport journalist Published 16 November 2026 Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season. The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season. He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real. The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup. "I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said. "Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years. "That may have affected my start to the season. "On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season." Learn about the VWP and ESTA and if your country participates in the program. How to request a travel authorization to the U.S. through ESTA If you find out your country participates in the Visa Waiver Program: Confirm that your passport meets the program requirements. You must have an electronic passport or “e-Passport” to participate in the VWP. This type of passport includes a chip. Complete the ESTA application online. Pay the fees: The total cost is $40.27. Learn about the payment options available to pay ESTA fees. When you complete and submit the form and processing fee, you will get an ESTA application number. Use that number to check your ESTA application status. It may take up to 72 hours to find out if you are authorized to travel to the U.S. under the VWP. At more than 2,500 feet, the Gocta waterfall, near the village of Cocachimba in northern Peru, is one of the world’s tallest. Ernesto Benavides By Heather Jasper Published October 20, 2026 Although the pre-Incan fortress of Kuélap is almost a thousand years older than Machu Picchu, it gets only a fraction of the crowds. The Chachapoya people built the citadel in northern Peru around the year 500 A.D. on a narrow fin of limestone high above the Utcubamba River—not unlike Machu Picchu’s perch above the Vilcanota River. Visit in 2027 to see new exhibits in the Apu Chuillaxa visitors’ center and walk a new trail in Malcapampa , an active archaeological site that has been newly opened to the public. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) When to Go The warm, rainy season arrives in the cloud forests of this part of Peru in November and lasts until April. More than a thousand orchid species are in bloom and the waterfalls thunder with extra volume. A cooler dry season from May through October offers better road conditions and drier trails, making it easier to visit archaeological sites around Kuélap.
